title: Introducing Yourself
label: ch:introductions
canDo: I can introduce myself in German, give my name, and understand the other person's name.

payoff.summary: Now a first real exchange — giving your name, asking for someone else's, and saying you are glad to meet them: Ich heiße Mira. — Wie heißen Sie? — Ich heiße Arun. — Freut mich. It is built the way the greetings were: each piece taken apart first, then assembled — and, because German is English's sibling, most of those pieces are direct English cousins. GE-C02-practice puts the four lines back together at the end.
payoff.note: Chapter 2 is now generated from schema-v2 lessons, so the payoff is atom-scored: GE-C02-practice runs every headword of the exchange and every cousin-root the chapter argued for. The pronunciation atoms and the two transferable grammar rules — the verb endings and verb-second — are drilled in their own lessons and are deliberately not claimed here.
